### Task 4: Docs + gate + PR

- [ ] **Step 4.1:** `docs/architecture/sessions-and-checkpoints.md`: extend the background-task section with the commit-linkage behavior (idle+markers → linkable; commit-snapshot capture backs the trailer; ordinary idle commits unaffected). One paragraph, matching style.
- [ ] **Step 4.2:** `mise run fmt && mise run lint && mise run test:ci` — all green.

**BUG — the marker bypass in `shouldCondenseWithOverlapCheck` isn't idle-only.** The condition `(isActive && isRecentInteraction) || hasLiveInFlightMarker` fires for ANY non-active session with a marker, including PhaseEnded. **Comment fix:** `addTrailerForAgentCommit`'s doc (~2153) says the IDLE+marker shape fires "regardless of TTY" — wrong; the `skipContentDetection` gate (noTTY || commit_linking=always) is computed before the eligibility loop, so a TTY + non-always session never reaches it. Reword accurately.

4. Cosmetic: the transcript's `FileChange` content (`"# Idle marker\n"`) and the actual `env.WriteFile` content differ. Nothing asserts on file content so it's harmless, but making them identical would remove a "wait, is this divergence intentional?" pause for future readers.

**Approved** — with issue 1 recommended as a pre-merge fix (trivial reorder; it only affects failure reporting, never produces a false pass) and issue 2 recommended before the PR lands so the orphan-prune gap gets a tracked home. Consolidates #1934 and #2003 into this one, so the checkpoint sync-destination work is a single review instead of three.

They overlap in files rather than conflicting: #1934 adds 62 lines to the same `checkpoint_sync_remote_test.go` the capture work restructures, and #2003 touches the same `doctor.go` as the note fix below. Both cherry-picked cleanly — git auto-merged every shared file — so this is about keeping one set of changes to the election in front of one reviewer, not about untangling a conflict. #2003 *was* conflicting against main (`checkpoint_read_confinement_test.go`, against #1951's changes) and needed the rebase either way; that resolution is described at the bottom.

One theme: **the push destination decides where checkpoints go, and the user can see what it decided.**

Trails: [1054](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/1054) (replay visibility), [996](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/996) (checkpoint_remote ownership).

---

## 1–2. Capture the election only on real delivery

Capture wrote the election as soon as it decided a push qualified, before the push ran. Six things between that decision and the data landing can stop delivery:

| Between gate and delivery | Before |
| --- | --- |
| Checkpoint policy diverged / unsupported | election moved, nothing delivered |
| OPF decision failed, or user aborted | election moved, nothing delivered |
| OPF rewrite failed | election moved, nothing delivered |
| Empty-remote defer (git-branch) | election moved, nothing delivered |
| Push rejected | election moved, nothing delivered |
| git-refs queue flush failed | election moved, nothing delivered |

Each printed `Checkpoints now sync to "X"` while X received nothing. The election is one-shot (*first capture sticks*), so the still-queued checkpoints could then only drain to the remote that had just refused them — recoverable only by hand-editing settings or deleting the state file.

**The likeliest way in needs no failure at all**: add a fresh empty fork and push your branch to it. That push declares the fork, so capture fired, and it is exactly the push the empty-remote defer suppresses (publishing `entire/checkpoints/v1` to a branchless remote lets a forge adopt it as the default branch).

Capture is now two-phase — propose, then persist after delivery. The gate takes the pending remote as a second argument so the electing push may carry the checkpoints that justify the election, and each backend commits at its own success point.

The second commit exists because the rejected-push test found the first one only half-fixed it: `doPushRef` is fail-soft by design and returns `nil` on **every** failure path, so "the push loop returned no error" was the wrong signal. `doPushRef`/`pushRefIfNeeded` now return `(delivered bool, err error)`, true only where `finishPush` runs. git-refs passed throughout; git-branch — the default — did not.

Essentially yes. The session's own transcript shows no `disable`/`clean`/`rm` — it was only *reading* `.entire/settings` and `.entire/redactors/` (support debugging) — so the deletion came from **outside the session**: something you ran in a terminal at ~09:38–09:39 yesterday morning in the `support` worktree removed `.entire/` (manual `rm`, `entire disable`, `clean`, or a re-setup — the freshly rewritten `settings.json` at 09:39 says an `enable`-style setup ran right after).

So the sequence was: your live Claude session's turn-start hook created/opened `.entire/tmp`, started its git-status walk, your deletion swept the directory out from under it mid-write, and the hook reported exactly what it should — a **non-blocking** failure — and the turn carried on. One turn's untracked-file baseline was lost; everything after self-healed (the hook recreates the dir next turn).

So: not a bug in any meaningful sense, not fixed by (or related to) any of the four open PRs, and expected behavior when `.entire/` is deleted under a live session. The only improvement available is cosmetic robustness — retry-once on ENOENT so the message never appears for this race. Happy to ship that as a two-line PR if the message bothers you; otherwise it's safe to ignore.
